notes: Supplied by the strand brief as OpenAlex W7128864510 only. opencite lookup cannot resolve a bare OpenAlex work identifier, so it was resolved through the OpenAlex REST interface, curl https://api.openalex.org/works/W7128864510, which returned title 'Brain4FMs: A Benchmark of Foundation Models for Electrical Brain Signal', publication_date 2026-02-12, type preprint, and primary_location landing_page_url http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11558. OpenAlex reports no DOI for the work, and no DataCite DOI was found, so doi is null. Author-name note: OpenAlex renders the second author as 'Yang Enhong'; the arXiv abs page and the PDF title block both give 'Enhong Yang', which is what the card and the bib use. Licence read directly from the abs-license block on the arXiv abs page, which links http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/ -- arXiv's default non-exclusive licence, conveying no third-party redistribution right. pdf_license is therefore unknown, redistribution_ok is false, and no PDF is committed. source.md is a markitdown conversion of the v1 PDF (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.11558, 3.51 MB, retrieved 2026-07-31), retained as internal research notes under fair use. md_quality is rough: the source is a two-column ACM-style paper, so body sentences from the two columns interleave line by line and inter-word spacing is stripped. Table 1 (the model inventory with parameter counts) survived as readable text and is the source of the checkpoint list on the card. The per-dataset results tables (Tables 3 to 5 and Tables 31 to 34) came out partially shredded, with metric columns split from their headers; only the values that also appear in surrounding prose or in an intact row are quoted on the card. Figures 1 to 4 are image-only and lost, including the benchmark-pipeline overview and the channel-permutation sensitivity plot. Appendix D, which holds the full results, is referenced but its tables are largely unreadable in the extraction. EXTRACTION UPDATE 2026-08-01 -- source.md was regenerated with pymupdf4llm, which preserves markdown tables and inter-word spacing that the earlier markitdown conversion destroyed, and md_quality was reassessed against the new extraction as clean (was rough). The PDF used for that extraction is cached locally as source.local.pdf, which is gitignored and deliberately not committed because the licence forbids redistribution.
